page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the high clock speed family. Powered by a KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Hardware support includes instruction sets such as AVX-512F, AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence, and supplies a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps without dedicated GPUs.

Performance evaluation highlights a divergence between single-threaded and parallel workloads. Benchmark results show weak single-core metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1095.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 1356.18. Conversely, multithreaded benchmarks fall consistently within the mid-tier cloud distribution. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 15463.52 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6654.0, supported by solid compilation throughput of 12381.0 in Clang tests. Memory subsystem testing shows read bandwidth of 73.32 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 38.81 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by Redis SET execution reaching 13.86 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 7.98 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation targets compute-bound applications rather than in-memory data platforms. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated accelerators limits its efficacy for heavy model training or extreme IOPS requirements, as demonstrated by low throughput on 7B LLM inference. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of dedicated compute threads without paying for surplus memory capacity. The instance profile is suited for multithreaded build automation, Clang software compilation, static web serving fleets, distributed batch processing, and moderate database services that operate comfortably within a 32 GB memory ceiling.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is a compute-focused instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an 8-core Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at 3.1 GHz, it incorporates instruction sets including AVX-512F and AES. The instance features no local storage and relies on a 3 Gbps baseline network link, with zero GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate modest single-thread efficiency counterbalanced by steady multi-core execution, registering 15463.52 in PassMark CPU and 6654.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory operations demonstrate stable throughput with 73.32 GB/sec uncached reads and 13.86 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking local storage, the 1:2 core-to-memory configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-skewed tasks by avoiding unused RAM overhead. It functions effectively for continuous integration pipelines, software compilation tasks, concurrent microservices, and web serving workloads.
